Subject: Performance SLO qualification - Veridian Analytics (post-call recap)

Thanks for taking the call today - recap and next steps below.

Summary of requirements (from today's call):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation < 250 ms for short assistant turns (~<128 tokens); p99 < 600 ms for long turns.
- Throughput: steady-state 200 QPS with ability to burst to 500 QPS for 10-30s during peak campaigns.
- Concurrency: target 50 concurrent model sessions; connection-oriented streaming for partial responses required for chat UX.
- Safety: no customer data leaves region; VPC/private deployment preferred for final production.

Cost / performance levers we discussed:
- Continuous batching + adaptive batch sizing to keep amortized GPU kernel time low while respecting latency SLOs.
- Prefix / KV caching for common system prompts and earlier conversation context to reduce repeated compute.
- Quantization profile: recommend testing 8-bit then 4-bit quantized weights for candidate model variants (int8/4bit LLMs) to reduce GPU memory and cost.
- Model variants: start with a high-quality quantized 13B variant for accuracy; fallback to smaller 7B-quant variants for tail-cost control.
- Dedicated capacity options for predictable latency; hosted with reserved pools if you want mix of predictability and managed ops.

Attachments: redwood-slo-playbook.pdf (high-level playbook), veridian-map.xlsx (mutual action plan - draft).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive w/ Rishi & infra team: benchmark config matrix (batch sizes, token-limits, quant profiles) - proposed slot Mon, May 3 at 10am PT.
2) Receive sample traffic profile (1-2 days of anonymized traces + typical prompt/response lengths) - Alex to share by Fri, Apr 30.
3) Redwood to deliver: rough TCO estimate + recommended config and SLO play (3 business days after receiving traces).

Let me know if I missed anything.

-
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - Veridian Analytics (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa - this is great, captured everything from our side. A couple clarifications:
- The p95 target of 250ms is for typical short assistant replies - ideal. For long generations (>512 tokens) we expect p95 around 1s, p99 under 2s - is that achievable with streaming?
- For throughput, 200 QPS is our avg for search workflows; during email campaigns we can see spikes similar to what you noted.

We'll share a scrubbed 48-hr traffic sample by tomorrow (Fri). Also attaching a quick internal note on expected token distribution.

One ask: can you include an estimated monthly spend at 200 QPS with the 13B quantized baseline and a conservative 4-bit fallback? A rough ballpark will help us with procurement.

Appreciate it - Alex

--
Alex Chen
Platform Lead, Veridian Analytics
alex.chen@veridiananalytics.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@veridiananalytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - Veridian Analytics (post-call recap)

Alex - quick technical notes / feasibility:
- Streaming: yes - we can stream tokens as they're generated; this actually helps perceived latency for users while allowing larger generations.
- Continuous batching + adaptive admission control: we'll target envelope where tail-latency meets p95 targets by limiting batch depth for low-latency paths and allowing larger batches for background/async jobs.
- Caching: prefix caching for system prompts and frequent user prompts should reduce effective compute by 10-30% depending on hit-rate; we should instrument sample traces to estimate hit rate.
- Quantization: int8 is safe for initial tests; ext4 (4-bit) can reduce cost substantially but requires validation on your eval suite. We'll run A/B quality checks.

I'll start a benchmark matrix (13B-quant, 7B-quant, int8 vs 4bit) and provide expected tokens/sec per GPU and estimated price per 1M tokens. Expect the initial matrix by Tue, May 4.

I'll also include a draft config for Dedicated vs Hosted reserved pool tradeoffs.

-
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
